reason: Three breadcrumb trails for three areas with different labels and links; parallel by design.
cli get/del delegate to request; web apiFetch is another package with token refresh.
The SSRF module's own layers (AGENTS.md lists both policies as shared); one range set already.
Pre-flight host check vs a socket lookup hook that pins the address; different jobs.
CSV export cell (formula guard) vs delimited data-type cell (no guard, message content must not change).
Export CSV with header vs the delimited data-type writer; same reason as G0009.
CLI padded table vs a research script's Markdown table.
getTlsBool reads the nested tls bag; AGENTS.md lists getTls* as the shared helpers.

Test Connection's requireNumber must refuse a missing or non-finite number with an error, while the form's getNum reads a stored bag and shows a fallback. The connectors' num also reads decimal text, because a ${name} configuration reference resolves to text at deploy; the form never sees resolved references, so it reads only finite numbers. All three refuse NaN and Infinity.

The server certificate resolver and the connectors each read the tls bag and refuse a non-object tls, so a channel cannot fall back to plaintext. They differ only in what an unset tls gives ({} in the resolver, undefined in the connectors) and in the error type (ServiceError INVALID_INPUT, Error).

readTlsServerOptions and readTlsClientOptions refuse a non-object tls and half a key pair, and a listener also needs both cert and key. readQueueTls and readHttpSourceTls are the registry's wrappers over them, gated on useTls and on the HTTP scheme. The other 15 members were judged DIFFERENT and are listed only so the group closes.
requireString is a server validator, databaseVendor and getTlsStr wrap getStr; listed shared helpers.
Server-side vs client-side TLS resolution; different required fields.
Soak script reads fields by raw split; standalone script, no workspace imports.
Private mode branches of the attachment extractor.
